launch_speed_band_note: 37.3-45.2 km/h from the preferred topspin model varying intrinsics +/-15% and camera tilt +/-5 deg; band floor extended to 25 km/h to cover the ballistic-only (no-spin) alternative interpretation (24.6-43.2 km/h), which fits the pixels but contradicts the measured ball apparent size

spin_accel_ms2.note: constant-accel Magnus approximation; ay<0 = topspin pressing the ball down (g_eff=16.0 m/s2). The clip caption literally says 'topspin shot'.

camera.note: world: X right, Y up, Z = optical-axis ground projection; camera at (0,h,0); solved jointly with trajectory

method_notes: Track: fused 3 independent 2D trackers (frame-diff, Hough/template, optical-flow), median-gated and confidence-weighted, frames 72-111 (37 obs after merging duplicated screen-recording frames 87/91/101 at midpoint timing). The camera inside the screen recording pans up to ~80 px (zoom negligible, scale 0.996-1.000), so every observation was mapped into the frame-71 camera via per-frame LK+RANSAC background stabilization before fitting. Model: p(t)=p0+v0*t+0.5*a*t^2, a=(ax, -(g-ay), az): constant-acceleration Magnus terms ax (side-spin) and ay (topspin), quadratic-drag az bounded <=0 (fit chose ~0). Both spin terms are data-driven: without ax the horizontal residual is an S-shaped 65 px (RMS 41.5 vs 12.0 px); without ay the fit cannot satisfy gravity timing and the measured ball apparent size simultaneously (they disagree ~30% in scale). With ay free, the fit converges to the ball-radius depth scale on its own (z0=3.7 m vs radius-implied 3.41 m), RMS 11.96 px (best of all variants), camera height 1.9 m (natural phone height), and ay=-6 m/s2 topspin - independently confirmed by the clip's own caption '[topspin shot ready]'. Anchors: p0 on the ground (y=0.11 m) at the pre-contact ball pixel; g=9.81 as timing ruler; pre-contact ball radius (41.7 px sharp, D=0.22 m) as depth ruler. Fitted ~6 m/s2 Magnus accelerations are 2-3x textbook values for ~11 m/s - they likely absorb some radius-measurement bias, so treat the spin split (vs speed) as qualitative. PLAUSIBILITY: launch ~3.6 m from camera, goal mouth reached ~9-10 m depth, apex ~0.95 m, flight 0.76 s. This is a short training free kick with heavy topspin into a close goal, NOT a 20-30 m match free kick, so the 60-110 km/h amateur free-kick range does not apply; 40 km/h (11 m/s) over a ~7 m carry is entirely plausible. Caveat: assumes the source clip is real-time; if it is slow-mo retimed, the true speed scales up by the retime factor.
flight_points_note: truncated at t=0.646 s (frame ~105) where the constant-topspin model crosses the ground; the real ball is still airborne at f111 (keeper save follows) - constant-acceleration Magnus overstates late dip because spin/speed decay; launch parameters are set by the early/mid arc and are unaffected
